MLforSEO Academy · The AI-powered Entity Audit

Entity Extractor & Salience Profiler

Pull entities out of your content with Google's Natural Language API, then roll them up into one profile per URL — so you can see which pages are about something other than what you intended.

What you need
A Google Cloud API key with the Cloud Natural Language API enabled
Cost
Free for most audits — 5,000 units a month, then $1 per 1,000
Feed it
Paste one page, or upload a crawl export with a URL column and a content column
You get back
entity_mentions.csv and page_entity_profiles.csv, plus entity_mentions_filtered.csv and filter_decisions.csv after the noise filters

How to use it

  1. Paste your API key. It stays in this browser tab and is sent only to Google.
  2. Start with a single page so you can see the shape of the data before spending anything.
  3. Set the intended entity — what the page is supposed to be about.
  4. Read the table: the top row is what a machine thinks the page is about.
  5. Then upload your whole crawl and export both CSVs.
  6. Apply the three noise filters: structural types, generic nouns, then site chrome. Review the chrome candidates, untick real topics, and export the filtered entities and the filter record.

Worth knowing. Use API version 1. Version 2 does not return a salience score at all, and every prominence measure here depends on it.

Noise filters

Applied in this order. Changing a filter re-runs it here; nothing is sent to Google again.

NUMBER, DATE, PRICE, ADDRESS and PHONE_NUMBER, plus names made only of digits. They are real entities, just not topics: a page that mentions “2026” forty times is not about the year 2026.

Words that turn up on every page of every site and say nothing about the topic. Edit the list for your site: one per line, or separated by commas.

Button and navigation text that survived inside your content block. An entity is a candidate when it is on a large share of your pages and never written as a proper noun. It needs both conditions; either one alone catches real topics.

% of pages

Chrome candidates: review each one

Ticked rows are removed. Untick anything that is a real topic on your site, because a focused site’s core topics are frequent too. If a real topic shows up here, you can also raise the share. If button labels still appear in the entity table below, lower it.
The record lists everything removed and every chrome candidate you kept. Save it with the audit.
